key_insight: Neutral ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces by removing excess tin, improving electron extraction and suppressing interfacial nonradiative recombination.
engineering_relevance: Controlling molecular protonation and surface defects offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free perovskite solar cells.
method: Compare surface reactions of neutral ethylenediamine and protonated ethylenediammonium iodide.
Use atomistic simulations to examine iodide migration and defect-assisted deprotonation.
Apply surface reconstruction to improve electron extraction into C60.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency and simulations showing that subsurface iodide vacancies lower the energetic cost of deprotonation.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish long-term operational stability or scalability of the surface treatment.
paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
